children: The euro is consolidating below $1.10 as the strong dollar dominates across the board, ING's Chris Turner says in a note. That said, price action in the euro-dollar currency pair "masks ongoing resilience on the macro side, where business confidence remains relatively high and better-than-expected eurozone growth rates this year are projected to continue into 2027," the analyst says. ING finds it hard to see the trend in the strong dollar turning before mid-December, and thinks the euro still risks a drop to the $1.0880 area, Turner says. The euro last trades stable at $1.0974 after reaching a 19-month low of $1.0952 Wednesday, LSEG data show. (emese.bartha@wsj.com)
